objective: Equity book v1.3 candidate: raise the net Sharpe of the unchanged v1.2 primary book M0_U3000 by trading cheaper. Five preregistered rules replace full rebalancing at each weekly tranche refresh: Garleanu-Pedersen partial adjustment at rate 1/2 (P2) or 1/3 (P3), the same on the unit book with the VIX scale applied at once (P2V), and a no-trade band of 0.25 or 0.50 cross-sectional weight SD (N25, N50; Novy-Marx-Velikov buy/hold analogue). A rule replaces B0 only if it clears the runbook optimization rule (+0.10 offset-median net Sharpe in both the recent and the stress window) plus a paired Newey-West t >= 2 and account-layer confirmation.
target_regime_and_horizon: Same as v1.2 (hypotheses.md section 7 there): US equities in the research U3000, weekly 5 tranches, decision at the close of D, fill at the close of D+1. The trading rule is regime-independent by construction (it changes how the book trades, not what it holds in steady state), so it must hold in both the recent window 2024-01-08..2026-09-15 and the stress window 2017-10-02..2023-08-31. Validity to 2026-12-31 with the v1.2 book; a replacement switches no earlier than the first monthly rescoring after the v1.2 two-week execution shakedown.
existing_solution_comparison: Published cost mitigation is mature and reused, not reinvented: GP 2013 (fixed-rate partial adjustment towards an aim; dynamic optimum net Sharpe 0.58 vs best static 0.46 vs Markowitz -9.84 in their futures test), NMV 2016 (buy/hold spread best: UMD-like 0.51%/month net vs 0.37 staggered rebalancing), JKMP (aim-portfolio ML book about 20% higher net Sharpe than a static two-stage alternative). v1.2 already uses staggered rebalancing (5 weekly tranches) and the engine drops orders below $100, which NMV rank below the buy/hold spread and which act as an implicit band only at the account level. What is missing is our own number: how much of v1.2's cost (224 bp a year recent, 152 bp stress, 26% of it on VIX-flip rebalances) can be saved before the delayed alpha costs more.
remaining_evidence_gap: The alpha decay of the M0 composite at 1-3 week delays and the turnover share that is pure drift or rank noise, which decide whether any rule nets +0.10; and whether the gain survives whole shares and the $100 minimum order in the account layer.
negative_experiments_checked: T-19 (80a82a6): the v1 optimizer lost about half the signal (transfer 0.41-0.51), so v1.3 keeps the simple R6 construction and only changes the trade from old to new weights; T-24 (e218e62): no new signal entered, so the composite stays M0; T-17 (t20260930_17): model family barely changes ranking skill and the 63-day horizon IC is about twice the 21-day IC on the price-volume panel, consistent with slow decay; v1.2 (412ef13): cost2x Sharpe 1.227 vs 1.506 shows the book's cost sensitivity. Registry check 2026-10-04 for turnover / partial rebalancing / transaction-cost-aware / no-trade band found only keyword collisions, no prior cost-mitigation experiment on the book.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Identical to v1.2 / T-25 R6 for the decision series: make_cost_fn('close') at E = $1M (half-spread + square-root impact + 0.5 bp fees per side, ETF branch for SPY), borrow 25 bp a year on short notional (R6 identity), costs charged on |x_new - x_old| of the drifted tranche and on the SPY hedge change; 2x cost replayed on the same paths and reported. Stage 2 account layer exactly as v1.2 (whole shares round-half-away, $100 minimum order, Alpaca margin table, F1 k 0.5 x VIX with T-bill leg and G 1.8, F2 SPY 1.0 plus overlay, borrow 0 bp ETB, cash 0%).
stop_condition: No rule meets E1 (+0.10 offset-median net Sharpe vs B0 in both windows) after Stage 1: keep v1.2 full rebalancing, write the frontier and the death cause, run no Stage 2. Stage 2 failure of any confirmation (other variants, account layer, family DSR tier, placebo): keep v1.2. No rate or band outside the five preregistered values is tried under this contract; the only follow-up is a new contract for a persistence-tilted aim (GP Proposition 3) designed from the return-free diagnostics.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Stage 1 of brief T-20261004-01 on the frozen research snapshot, local, run_capped 1.8G, one process: B0 identity against data/research/equity_book/realism_ladder/R6_M0_U3000_o<k>.parquet (<= 1e-12), then P2, P3, P2V, N25, N50 on M0_U3000 for the 5 offsets (25 strategy-level passes, about 1 minute each), metrics in both windows and the E1-E4 eligibility table.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one rule meets E1 (offset-median net Sharpe >= B0 + 0.10 in both the recent 2024-01-08..2026-09-15 and the stress 2017-10-02..2023-08-31 window), E2 (>= 4 of 5 offsets improve in each window), E3 (paired Newey-West t, lag 5, of the blended daily net difference >= 2 over 2017-10-02..2026-09-15) and E4 (|realized beta| <= 0.15 in both windows); then Stage 2 confirmations decide replacement.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: No rule meets E1-E4: cost-aware trading of the unchanged composite cannot clear the optimization rule; v1.2 keeps full rebalancing and the frontier plus death cause are recorded.

sources.claim: Garleanu and Pedersen (NBER w15205, 2009; Journal of Finance 2013): with predictable returns and transaction costs the optimal policy trades partially towards an aim portfolio at a fixed rate a/lambda < 1 that falls with costs and rises with risk aversion (Proposition 2, eq. 7-10); the aim is an exponential average of current and expected future Markowitz portfolios, so predictors with slower alpha decay get more weight (Proposition 3). In their commodity-futures application (Table II, benchmark costs) the Markowitz portfolio has gross Sharpe 0.83 and net -9.84, the dynamic optimum 0.62 gross / 0.58 net, and the best static partial-adjustment rule (3% weight on Markowitz per day) 0.58 / 0.46; the dynamic net Sharpe is about 20% above the best static strategy because it under-weights the fast (2.4-day half-life) signal.
sources.core_claim: Garleanu and Pedersen (NBER w15205, 2009; Journal of Finance 2013): with predictable returns and transaction costs the optimal policy trades partially towards an aim portfolio at a fixed rate a/lambda < 1 that falls with costs and rises with risk aversion (Proposition 2, eq. 7-10); the aim is an exponential average of current and expected future Markowitz portfolios, so predictors with slower alpha decay get more weight (Proposition 3). In their commodity-futures application (Table II, benchmark costs) the Markowitz portfolio has gross Sharpe 0.83 and net -9.84, the dynamic optimum 0.62 gross / 0.58 net, and the best static partial-adjustment rule (3% weight on Markowitz per day) 0.58 / 0.46; the dynamic net Sharpe is about 20% above the best static strategy because it under-weights the fast (2.4-day half-life) signal.
sources.market_and_period: Commodity futures 1996-2009 (NBER working-paper version), daily data, quadratic transaction costs
sources.applicability: Rules P2, P3 and P2V are the static fixed-rate form of Proposition 2 applied per tranche to the unchanged M0 target; the persistence-tilted aim (Proposition 3) is deferred to a later contract because it changes the composite.
sources.limitations: Commodity futures, daily data, quadratic costs and a 5-day signal; our book is weekly, mostly slow signals, with spread plus square-root impact, so the size of the gain does not transfer, only the form of the rule.
sources.independent_replication: JKMP (SFI 22-63) extends the same aim-portfolio solution to stock portfolios with ML forecasts (eq. 20-21) and reports a net Sharpe about 20% above a two-stage static alternative; no independent replication on a weekly rank-weighted U3000 book was found.

sources.claim: Novy-Marx and Velikov (A Taxonomy of Anomalies and Their Trading Costs, August 2015 version; RFS 2016), 1973-2012 with effective-spread costs: a buy/hold spread (a stricter rule to enter a position than to keep it, e.g. 10%/20% deciles) is the most effective cost-mitigation technique; for a UMD-like factor it earns 0.77%/month gross, 0.26% costs, 0.51% net, against 0.62 / 0.26 / 0.37 for staggered quarterly partial rebalancing and 0.66 / 0.35 / 0.31 for trading only a low-cost universe (Table 5): the same cost saving as lower-frequency staggered rebalancing while giving up less gross return.

sources.applicability: Rules N25 and N50 are the continuous-weight analogue (a no-trade band around each name's target); v1.2's five weekly tranches are already a form of staggered partial rebalancing, which this paper ranks below the buy/hold spread.
